# Purpose

The preferred model of `weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` gives every country the
response of the climate gradient at its long-run climate. This notebook starts
from that model with long-run income in the interaction (the preferred
specification here) and asks how far each country's own response departs from
the gradient, how precisely it is known, and how the country responses can be
estimated and used:

1. the preferred specification: linear arms of the horizon deviations of
   temperature and precipitation, each arm interacted with the unit's
   long-run climate and income;
2. the mixed model: each country's own coefficients (step 1), regressed on
   long-run climate and income allowing for a spread of the true country
   responses around the gradient (step 2, a random-effects meta-regression);
   the country responses that follow (BLUPs) and their precision;
3. the analyses built on them (from "Further analyses" on).

The data, the sample and the specification are those of
`weather_arms_robustness.Rmd` ("Data and methods"), with the same code; this
notebook repeats only what it needs. Effects are in percentage points (pp) of
the annual growth of GDP per capita for one year at +3 or -3 SD against a year
at the unit's trend; `dT+`, `dT-` (`dP+`, `dP-`) are the positive and negative
arms, both positive numbers; stars are \*\*\* p < 0.01, \*\* p < 0.05,
\* p < 0.1.

# Data and specification

**Data.** GDP per capita from the Penn World Table 11.0 (`rgdpna / pop`,
constant national prices at the 2021 PPP level; the main panel, PWT x ERA5)
and, for the regions, DOSE v2.14 (`r params$dose_variable`, constant 2015 local
prices at the 2015 exchange rate: no movements of the exchange rate). The
outcome is the growth of GDP per capita, the difference of its logarithm
between consecutive calendar years (a gap gives a missing growth rate; nothing
is interpolated, extrapolated or converted). Annual temperature `TM` (°C) and
precipitation `RR` (m) from ERA5 in the Weighted Climate Dataset, aggregated
with population-density weights at base year 2000. Conflict indicators (UCDP/PRIO:
minor conflict, war) and the post-Soviet and post-Yugoslav collapse-year
dummies are the controls.

**Regression.** Year effects, unit effects and unit linear and quadratic
trends (t = year - 1990), as in Burke, Hsiang and Miguel (2015); OLS with the
fixed effects absorbed; errors clustered by country:

```text
g(i,t) = weather terms(i,t) + c1 minor conflict + c2 war + collapse-year dummies
         + unit effect(i) + unit trend(i) x t + unit quadratic trend(i) x t^2 + year effect(t) + error
```

**Deviations.** Against the horizon baseline (the unit's mean and SD of the
variable over `r params$start_year` to the last year of the panel), demeaned
(the unit's mean and linear and quadratic trend removed), then cut into arms:

```text
dT = (TM - mean) / SD       dm = dT - (unit mean + linear and quadratic trend)
dT+ = max(dm, 0)            dT- = max(-dm, 0)                      (the same for P)
```

**Growth outliers.** The 5% lowest and 5% highest growth rates of PWT x ERA5
from the start year, each annotated with its likely cause; those whose cause
does not involve weather are dropped, from every panel (in DOSE from every
region of the country).

**Comparing models.** Where models are compared by AIC, BIC or the within
adjusted R2, the verdict is "indifferent" when the difference cannot be told
apart from noise (clustered Vuong test, or the Wald test of the added terms
for nested models, 5%).

```{r shared-specification}
# As in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd (shared-specification).
START_YEAR <- as.integer(params$start_year)
CLIMATE_WEIGHT <- "population density"
CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR <- 2000L

OUTCOME <- "dlgrp_pc_usd"
# Year effects, unit effects and unit linear and quadratic trends (t = year -
# 1990, t2 = t^2), as in BHM (2015), in every model.
FIXED_EFFECTS <- "year + GID_1[t, t2]"

# The panels keep MAX_LAGS earlier climate years and the demeaning covers them
# (as in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd, so the deviations are the same).
MAX_LAGS <- 10L

# The UCDP/PRIO conflict indicators by the highest intensity of the country's
# conflicts that year (functions/conflict.R): conflict_low, minor (25-999
# battle deaths), and conflict_high, war (1,000 or more); and the post-Soviet
# (with Albania) and post-Yugoslav collapse-year dummies
# (functions/transition_collapse.R). National, so the same for every region of
# a country in the subnational panel.
CONFLICT_TERMS <- c("conflict_low", "conflict_high")
CONTROLS <- c(
  CONFLICT_TERMS,
  "i(fsu_collapse_year, ref = 'none')",
  "i(yug_collapse_year, ref = 'none')"
)

# Growth outliers: the 5% lowest and the 5% highest growth rates of GDP per
# capita of PWT x ERA5 from the start year (found in the panel-builder chunk),
# each with its likely cause, annotated by hand in
# data/growth_outlier_causes.csv and data/growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv;
# every country-year of the tails must have one. Dropped: those whose cause does
# not involve weather (including those with no identified cause). They are
# events of a country and year, so they are dropped from every panel (in DOSE,
# from every region of the country).
OUTLIER_SHARE <- 0.10
OUTLIER_CAUSES <- bind_rows(
  utils::read.csv(data_file("growth_outlier_causes.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  utils::read.csv(data_file("growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(OUTLIER_CAUSES[, c("GID_0", "year")]))

# Moments of the two deviation definitions: over the horizon of the panel
# (*_all, replaced below) and over the 20 years before the current one.
MOMENTS <- c(
  "mean_TM_all", "sd_TM_all", "mean_RR_all", "sd_RR_all",
  "mean_TM_lag_20", "sd_TM_lag_20", "mean_RR_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20"
)
# The demeaned deviations of each variable and baseline (built by prepare_panel()).
BASELINES <- c("all", "lag_20")
DEMEANED <- as.vector(outer(c("TM", "RR"), BASELINES, function(v, b) paste0("dm_", v, "_", b)))

fit_model <- function(terms, model_data, fixed_effects = FIXED_EFFECTS, outcome = OUTCOME) {
  m <- fit_panel_model(
    paste(terms, collapse = " + "),
    model_data,
    outcome = outcome,
    fixed_effects = fixed_effects,
    cluster = ~GID_0
  )
  # The country of each estimation row, for the noise tests of differences in fit.
  m$country <- model_data$GID_0[fixest::obs(m)]
  m
}

# Labels for the coefficient tables; the collapse dummies are left out of them.
DICT <- c(
  conflict_low = "Conflict, minor", conflict_high = "Conflict, war",
  clim_TM = "mean T", clim_RR = "mean P", inc = "income",
  devTM_pos = "dT+", devTM_neg = "dT-", devRR_pos = "dP+", devRR_neg = "dP-"
)
DROP <- "collapse_year"
# Temperature terms, then precipitation terms, then the controls (original names).
ORDER <- c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^conflict")
FITSTAT <- ~n + wr2 + aic + bic
```

The sample is the unit-years with growth, both weather variables, the
conflict indicators and the moments of the deviations (positive SDs), without
the non-weather growth outliers. The tables describe the main panel and count
its growth outliers by cause.

```{r panel-builder}
# As in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd (panel-builder), for PWT x ERA5 and DOSE x ERA5.
# Panel `econ` x `source` from `start_year`, with the horizon moments, the
# controls, the sample with and without the country-years `drop`, the rows
# dropped, and every unit-year of the panel (`data`, for lags of the weather).
prepare_panel <- function(econ, source, econ_variable = NULL, drop = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
                          start_year = START_YEAR) {
  cfg <- panel_config(
    econ_year_min = start_year,
    climate_source = source,
    climate_weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT,
    climate_weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
    # Eleven earlier climate years: up to ten carry the lags of the deviations
    # into the first years, one the lagged trailing moments. The sample starts
    # at start_year regardless.
    clim_history_years = 11L
  )
  data <- suppressMessages(build_dat(econ_data = econ, config = cfg,
                                     econ_variable = econ_variable))
  level <- unique(data$gadm_level)
  end_year <- max(data$year[est_row(data) & !is.na(data$TM) & !is.na(data$RR)])

  horizon <- load_climate_panel(level, cfg) %>%
    filter(gadm_level == level, year >= start_year, year <= end_year) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_TM_all = mean(TM, na.rm = TRUE), sd_TM_all = sd(TM, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_RR_all = mean(RR, na.rm = TRUE), sd_RR_all = sd(RR, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  data <- data %>%
    select(-c(mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all)) %>%
    left_join(horizon, by = "GID_1")
  data <- add_yugoslav_collapse(add_soviet_collapse(add_conflict(data)))
  data$TM2 <- data$TM^2
  data$RR2 <- data$RR^2
  data$t <- data$year - 1990L
  data$t2 <- data$t^2

  # Demeaned deviations: each unit's mean and quadratic trend removed.
  window <- data$year >= start_year - MAX_LAGS & data$year <= end_year
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (b in BASELINES) {
    raw <- (data[[v]] - data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", b)]]) / data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", b)]]
    ok <- which(window & is.finite(raw))
    sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = data$GID_1[ok], t = data$t[ok], t2 = data$t2[ok], x = raw[ok])
    m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
    demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
    demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
    data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", b)]] <- demeaned
  }

  complete <- stats::complete.cases(
    as.data.frame(data)[, c(OUTCOME, "TM", "RR", CONFLICT_TERMS, MOMENTS, DEMEANED)]
  )
  positive_sd <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(grep("^sd_", MOMENTS, value = TRUE), function(x) {
    !is.na(data[[x]]) & data[[x]] > 0
  }))
  sample_all <- data[est_row(data) & data$year >= start_year & complete & positive_sd, ]
  apply_exclusions(list(
    label = paste(econ, "x", source), econ = econ, source = source, level = level,
    start_year = start_year, end_year = end_year, all = sample_all, data = data
  ), drop)
}

# The sample of panel `p` without the country-years `drop` (clean), and the
# rows dropped (outliers).
apply_exclusions <- function(p, drop) {
  dropped <- paste(p$all$GID_0, p$all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  p$clean <- p$all[!dropped, ]
  p$outliers <- p$all[dropped, c("GID_0", "GID_1", "year", OUTCOME)]
  p
}

# (The argument is not called `panel`: tibble() would mask it with the column.)
panel_summary <- function(p) {
  tibble::tibble(
    panel = p$label,
    first_year = min(p$clean$year), last_year = max(p$clean$year),
    countries = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_0), units = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_1),
    observations = nrow(p$all), outliers_dropped = nrow(p$outliers),
    minor_conflict = sum(p$clean$conflict_low), war = sum(p$clean$conflict_high)
  )
}

# The outliers are the growth tails of the main panel (PWT x ERA5) from the
# start year, so it is built first, without exclusions. Every country-year of
# the tails must have an annotated cause.
main <- prepare_panel("PWT", "ERA5", drop = OUTLIER_CAUSES[0, c("GID_0", "year")])
cutoffs <- stats::quantile(main$all[[OUTCOME]], c(OUTLIER_SHARE / 2, 1 - OUTLIER_SHARE / 2),
                           names = FALSE)
tails <- main$all[main$all[[OUTCOME]] < cutoffs[[1]] | main$all[[OUTCOME]] > cutoffs[[2]], ]
country_year <- function(d) paste(d$GID_0, d$year)
stopifnot(all(country_year(tails) %in% country_year(OUTLIER_CAUSES)))
OUTLIERS <- OUTLIER_CAUSES[country_year(OUTLIER_CAUSES) %in% country_year(tails), ]
OUTLIERS_DROPPED <- OUTLIERS[OUTLIERS$weather == "no", c("GID_0", "year")]
main <- apply_exclusions(main, OUTLIERS_DROPPED)
dose <- prepare_panel("DOSE", "ERA5", econ_variable = params$dose_variable)

bind_rows(panel_summary(main), panel_summary(dose)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "The panels (unit-years; conflict after outliers)")
OUTLIERS %>%
  mutate(tail = ifelse(paste(GID_0, year) %in% paste(tails$GID_0[tails[[OUTCOME]] < 0],
                                                    tails$year[tails[[OUTCOME]] < 0]),
                       "low", "high"),
         status = ifelse(weather == "yes", "kept (weather)", "dropped")) %>%
  count(category, status, tail) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tail, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(status, desc(low + high)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Growth outliers of PWT x ERA5 from %d (growth below %.1f%% or above %.1f%%) by likely",
    "cause; see data/growth_outlier_causes.csv and data/growth_outlier_causes_1970_additions.csv"),
    START_YEAR, 100 * cutoffs[[1]], 100 * cutoffs[[2]]))
```

```{r model-helpers}
# As in weather_arms_robustness.Rmd (model-helpers and income-interaction), the
# helpers used here.
# Deviation terms of the demeaned deviations dm_<v>_<suffix>, with one suffix
# per variable (a definition, see DEFINITIONS), and the long-run climate they
# are interacted with, clim_<v> = mean_<v>_<suffix[["clim_<v>"]]>.
add_deviation_terms <- function(model_data, suffix) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    dev <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]] <- dev
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)^2
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)^2
    clim <- paste0("clim_", v)
    model_data[[clim]] <- model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", suffix[[clim]])]]
  }
  model_data
}
definition <- function(TM, RR, matched = FALSE) {
  c(TM = TM, RR = RR, clim_TM = if (matched) TM else "all", clim_RR = if (matched) RR else "all")
}
DEFINITIONS <- list("Horizon" = definition("all", "all"), "20-year" = definition("lag_20", "lag_20"))
FORMS <- list(
  "Linear arms" = list(TM = c("_pos", "_neg"), RR = c("_pos", "_neg")),
  "Quadratic arms" = list(TM = c("_pos2", "_neg2"), RR = c("_pos2", "_neg2"))
)
PREFERRED_DEFINITION <- params$preferred_definition
PREFERRED_FORM <- params$preferred_form
stopifnot(PREFERRED_DEFINITION %in% names(DEFINITIONS), PREFERRED_FORM %in% names(FORMS))

form_terms <- function(form) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    x <- paste0("dev", v, form[[v]])
    c(x, paste0(x, ":clim_", v))
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}
# Value of a deviation term (by column suffix) at deviations x.
term_value <- function(suffix, x) {
  if (suffix == "") return(x)
  switch(suffix, "_pos" = pmax(x, 0), "_neg" = pmax(-x, 0),
         "_pos2" = pmax(x, 0)^2, "_neg2" = pmax(-x, 0)^2)
}
interaction_name <- function(a, b, terms) {
  intersect(c(paste0(a, ":", b), paste0(b, ":", a)), terms)[[1]]
}
wald_p <- function(m, pattern) fixest::wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p
stars <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.01, "***", ifelse(p < 0.05, "**", ifelse(p < 0.1, "*", "")))

# Differences in fit against noise (see weather_arms_robustness.Rmd): a Vuong
# test clustered by country for non-nested models, the clustered Wald test of
# the added terms for nested ones; "indifferent" when not beyond noise at 5%.
NOISE_LEVEL <- 0.05
CRITERIA <- c(aic = "AIC", bic = "BIC", r2 = "within adj. R2")
fit_record <- function(m) {
  e <- stats::resid(m)
  s2 <- mean(e^2)
  list(aic = stats::AIC(m), bic = stats::BIC(m), war2 = fixest::fitstat(m, "war2")[[1]],
       n = stats::nobs(m), ll = -0.5 * log(2 * pi * s2) - e^2 / (2 * s2), country = m$country)
}
as_record <- function(x) if (inherits(x, "fixest")) fit_record(x) else x
criterion_value <- function(rec, criterion) {
  switch(criterion, aic = -rec$aic / 2, bic = -rec$bic / 2, r2 = -(rec$n / 2) * log(1 - rec$war2))
}
fit_verdict <- function(a, b, criterion, nested_p = NULL) {
  a <- as_record(a)
  b <- as_record(b)
  stopifnot(a$n == b$n, identical(a$country, b$country))
  difference <- criterion_value(a, criterion) - criterion_value(b, criterion)
  beyond_noise <- if (!is.null(nested_p)) {
    !is.na(nested_p) && nested_p < NOISE_LEVEL
  } else {
    D <- tapply(a$ll - b$ll, a$country, sum)
    G <- length(D)
    se <- sqrt(G / (G - 1) * sum((D - mean(D))^2))
    is.finite(se) && se > 0 && abs(difference / se) >= stats::qnorm(1 - NOISE_LEVEL / 2)
  }
  if (!beyond_noise) "indifferent" else if (difference > 0) "better" else "worse"
}
fit_verdicts <- function(a, b, nested_p = NULL) {
  a <- as_record(a)
  b <- as_record(b)
  paste(vapply(names(CRITERIA), function(cr) fit_verdict(a, b, cr, nested_p), ""),
        collapse = " / ")
}
added_terms_p <- function(larger, smaller) {
  added <- setdiff(names(stats::coef(larger)), names(stats::coef(smaller)))
  stopifnot(length(added) > 0, all(names(stats::coef(smaller)) %in% names(stats::coef(larger))))
  b <- stats::coef(larger)[added]
  V <- stats::vcov(larger)[added, added, drop = FALSE]
  stats::pchisq(as.numeric(t(b) %*% solve(V, b)), df = length(added), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
VERDICT_NOTE <- paste(
  "verdict by AIC / BIC / within adjusted R2: indifferent when the difference cannot be told",
  "apart from noise (clustered Vuong test, or the Wald test of the added terms for nested",
  "models, 5%)")

# Deviations (SD) and long-run climates (C, m a year) at which the effects are
# evaluated.
EFFECT_AT <- c(-3, 3)
EVAL_CLIMATE <- list(TM = c(5, 15, 25), RR = c(0.5, 1.5, 3))
EVAL_LABELS <- list(TM = c("5 °C", "15 °C", "25 °C"), RR = c("0.5 m", "1.5 m", "3 m"))

# Each unit's long-run income over the horizon of panel `p`, centred at the mean
# over the rows `d`.
add_income <- function(p, d) {
  income <- p$data %>%
    filter(year >= p$start_year, year <= p$end_year, !is.na(grp_pc_usd)) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(inc_level = log(mean(grp_pc_usd)), .groups = "drop")
  d <- left_join(d, income, by = "GID_1")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(d$inc_level))
  d$inc <- d$inc_level - mean(d$inc_level)
  d
}
# Weights on the coefficients `terms` of a deviation x (SD) of variable v in a
# model with the arms `suffixes`, at the values `modifiers` (named: the
# variables interacted with every deviation term, e.g. clim_TM, inc).
deviation_weights <- function(terms, suffixes, v, x, modifiers) {
  w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
  for (s in suffixes) {
    term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
    w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
    for (z in names(modifiers)) {
      w[[interaction_name(term, z, terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * modifiers[[z]]
    }
  }
  w
}
# Effects (pp, 95% CI) of EFFECT_AT SD of each variable at each long-run
# climate of EVAL_CLIMATE in model m (arms `form`), at the extra modifiers
# `at` (e.g. list(inc = 0)).
effects_at <- function(m, form, at = list()) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]), deviation = EFFECT_AT)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
      mods <- c(stats::setNames(list(EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]][[g]]), paste0("clim_", v)), at)
      deviation_weights(terms, form[[v]], v, x, mods)
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(m, G) %>%
      mutate(variable = v, level = EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}
effect_cell <- function(e) {
  sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", 100 * e$estimate, 100 * e$conf_low, 100 * e$conf_high,
          stars(e$p_value))
}
effect_row <- function(e) paste0(ifelse(e$variable == "TM", "T ", "P "),
                                 sprintf("%+d SD, ", e$deviation), e$level)
coef_cell <- function(e, se) sprintf("%.3g (%.2g)", e, se)
pp_interval <- function(e, lo, hi) sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", 100 * e, 100 * lo, 100 * hi)
```

# Preferred specification

Linear arms of the horizon deviations of temperature and precipitation, each
arm interacted with the unit's long-run climate and with its long-run income:

```text
growth = sum over arms a of  dev_a x (c_a + b_a clim + h_a inc)  + controls + FE
clim   = the unit's horizon mean of the variable (°C for T, m a year for P)
inc    = log of the unit's mean GDP per capita over the horizon (every year with
         GDP), minus its mean over the sample rows
```

Income is centred, so `c_a + b_a clim` is the response at the sample's average
income. The model without income (the preferred model of
`weather_arms_robustness.Rmd`) is shown for comparison, on the same rows. On
`r main$label`:

1. long-run income and climate across the units, by third of income;
2. the coefficients with and without the income terms;
3. the joint tests: the income terms, the climate interactions with and
   without income, and the verdict of the model with income against the one
   without;
4. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate: without income, at
   the average income and at the mean income of each third.

```{r preferred-model}
preferred_data <- add_income(main, add_deviation_terms(main$clean, DEFINITIONS[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]]))
preferred_form <- FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]
income_interactions <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  paste0("dev", v, preferred_form[[v]], ":inc")
}))
preferred_models <- list(
  "without income" = fit_model(form_terms(preferred_form), preferred_data),
  "with income" = fit_model(c(form_terms(preferred_form), income_interactions), preferred_data)
)
preferred <- preferred_models[["with income"]]

# 1. Income and climate across the units.
income_units <- distinct(preferred_data, GID_1, inc_level, clim_TM, clim_RR)
income_thirds <- income_units %>%
  mutate(third = factor(c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")[dplyr::ntile(inc_level, 3)],
                        levels = c("poorest third", "middle third", "richest third")))
income_thirds %>%
  group_by(third) %>%
  summarise(units = n(), gdp_pc = round(exp(mean(inc_level))),
            mean_T = round(mean(clim_TM), 1), mean_P = round(mean(clim_RR), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, units by third of long-run income: GDP per capita (geometric mean) and mean long-run",
    "climate; across the units, correlation of log income with mean T %.2f, with mean P %.2f"),
    main$label, stats::cor(income_units$inc_level, income_units$clim_TM),
    stats::cor(income_units$inc_level, income_units$clim_RR)))

# 2. Coefficients.
etable(unname(preferred_models), headers = names(preferred_models), dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations"))

# 3. Joint tests.
income_p <- added_terms_p(preferred, preferred_models[["without income"]])
tibble::tibble(
  test = c("income terms, all", "income terms, T", "income terms, P",
           "climate interactions with income, T", "climate interactions with income, P",
           "climate interactions without income, T", "climate interactions without income, P",
           "with income against without (AIC / BIC / R2)"),
  result = c(signif(income_p, 2), signif(wald_p(preferred, "^devTM.*:inc$|^inc:devTM"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(preferred, "^devRR.*:inc$|^inc:devRR"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(preferred, "clim_TM"), 2), signif(wald_p(preferred, "clim_RR"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(preferred_models[["without income"]], "clim_TM"), 2),
             signif(wald_p(preferred_models[["without income"]], "clim_RR"), 2),
             fit_verdicts(preferred, preferred_models[["without income"]], nested_p = income_p))
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": joint Wald tests (p) and the ", VERDICT_NOTE))

# 4. Effects at each climate, with and without income.
income_at <- c(list("without income" = NULL, "average income" = 0),
               lapply(split(income_thirds$inc_level, income_thirds$third),
                      function(x) mean(x) - mean(preferred_data$inc_level)))
names(income_at)[3:5] <- paste("income of the", names(income_at)[3:5])
preferred_effects <- lapply(names(income_at), function(k) {
  if (is.null(income_at[[k]])) {
    effects_at(preferred_models[["without income"]], preferred_form)
  } else {
    effects_at(preferred, preferred_form, list(inc = income_at[[k]]))
  }
})
tibble::tibble(effect = effect_row(preferred_effects[[1]])) %>%
  bind_cols(stats::setNames(lapply(preferred_effects, effect_cell), names(income_at))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ":"), "effect (pp, 95% CI) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate, without",
    "the income terms and, with them, at the average income and at the mean income of each",
    "third; *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

The figures show the response of growth to a deviation from -3 to +3 SD in the
model with income, in each cell of units by third of long-run climate (rows:
cold, temperate, hot; dry, mid, wet) and third of long-run income (columns), at
the mean climate and income of the cell's units; against it, the model without
income at the same climate. Each panel gives the number of units in the cell
and its mean climate; the bands are 95% CIs (clustered by country).

```{r preferred-model-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
INCOME_CURVE_X <- seq(-3, 3, by = 0.1)
CLIMATE_THIRDS <- list(TM = c("cold", "temperate", "hot"), RR = c("dry", "mid", "wet"))
# Cells of units by third of long-run climate and of income: units, mean
# climate and mean centred income.
income_cells <- bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
  clim <- paste0("clim_", v)
  income_thirds %>%
    mutate(climate_third = factor(CLIMATE_THIRDS[[v]][dplyr::ntile(.data[[clim]], 3)],
                                  levels = CLIMATE_THIRDS[[v]])) %>%
    group_by(climate_third, third) %>%
    summarise(units = n(), climate = mean(.data[[clim]]),
              inc = mean(inc_level) - mean(preferred_data$inc_level), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(variable = v)
}))
# Effect (pp) of the deviations INCOME_CURVE_X of variable v in model m at the
# values `mods`, with its 95% CI.
curve_at <- function(m, v, mods) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(m))
  G <- t(vapply(INCOME_CURVE_X, function(x) {
    deviation_weights(terms, preferred_form[[v]], v, x, mods)
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(m, G) %>%
    transmute(x = INCOME_CURVE_X, estimate = 100 * estimate, conf_low = 100 * conf_low,
              conf_high = 100 * conf_high)
}
income_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(income_cells)), function(i) {
  cell <- income_cells[i, ]
  clim <- stats::setNames(list(cell$climate), paste0("clim_", cell$variable))
  bind_rows(
    curve_at(preferred, cell$variable, c(clim, list(inc = cell$inc))) %>%
      mutate(model = "with income"),
    curve_at(preferred_models[["without income"]], cell$variable, clim) %>%
      mutate(model = "without income")
  ) %>%
    mutate(variable = cell$variable, climate_third = cell$climate_third, third = cell$third)
})) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("with income", "without income")))
INCOME_COLOURS <- grid_colours(c("with income", "without income"))
for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
  cells <- filter(income_cells, variable == v) %>%
    mutate(label = sprintf("%d units, %s", units,
                           if (v == "TM") sprintf("%.1f °C", climate) else sprintf("%.2f m", climate)))
  p <- ggplot(filter(income_curves, variable == v), aes(x, estimate, colour = model, fill = model)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(linetype = model), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = cells, aes(x = -3, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, colour = "grey30") +
    facet_grid(climate_third ~ third) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = INCOME_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = INCOME_COLOURS, name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "longdash"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3) +
    labs(x = paste(if (v == "TM") "Temperature" else "Precipitation",
                   "deviation (horizon SD, demeaned)"),
         y = "Effect on growth of GDP per capita (pp)",
         title = paste(if (v == "TM") "Temperature" else "Precipitation",
                       "response by long-run climate and income"),
         subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION,
                           " deviations; rows: third of long-run climate, columns: third of ",
                           "long-run income;\neach panel at its units' mean climate and income; ",
                           "bands: 95% CI, clustered by country")) +
    theme_results() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  print(p)
}
```

# The mixed model

The confidence intervals above are the uncertainty of the gradient
`c_a + b_a clim + h_a inc`, the mean response of the countries with a climate
and an income; they assume that every such country responds as the gradient
says. Each country's response is estimated on its own, and the country
responses are regressed on climate and income allowing for a spread around the
gradient (a random-effects meta-regression):

```text
step 1: growth = sum over arms a of  dev_a x beta_a(i)  + controls + FE
        (one coefficient per country and arm, the arms and rows of the preferred
        specification; heteroskedasticity-robust variances v_a(i), since a
        coefficient of a single country cannot be clustered by country)
step 2: beta_a(i) = c_a + b_a clim(i) + h_a inc(i) + u_a(i),   u_a(i) ~ N(0, tau_a^2)
        estimated by REML with sampling variances v_a(i) (metafor::rma)
```

`tau_a` is the spread of the true country responses around the gradient that
climate and income do not explain (I2: the share of the variance of the
country estimates it accounts for; the rest is sampling noise). A confidence
interval of the gradient uses only the uncertainty of the gradient; a
prediction interval adds `tau_a^2`, and is the interval for a country with that
climate and income. A country's own response (its BLUP) is the gradient at its
climate and income plus its estimated deviation `u`, which shrinks its own
estimate toward the gradient with the weight `tau^2 / (tau^2 + v)` on its own
estimate. Each country-arm enters step 2 if the arm is non-zero in at least
`MIN_ARM_YEARS` of its years (a coefficient from a handful of years has an
unreliable robust variance). The meta-regression on climate alone is shown for
comparison. On `r main$label`:

1. each arm: the gradient of the pooled model (the preferred specification)
   and of the meta-regression, with and without income; `tau`, I2, the share of
   `tau^2` that income explains, and the meta-regression with income against
   the one without (ML fits: AIC, BIC and the likelihood-ratio test);
2. the effects of a +/-3 SD year at each long-run climate at the average
   income: the pooled model's CI, the meta-regression's CI and its prediction
   interval;
3. figure: the country estimates moved to the average income, the gradient at
   the average income, its CI and the prediction interval;
4. the countries whose own response is most and least precise;
5. table and figure: the own response of India, Brazil, the United States and
   China in the country's own coefficients, the mixed model and the pooled
   model.

```{r mixed-model}
MIN_ARM_YEARS <- 10
EVENT_SD <- max(EFFECT_AT)
# The arms of `form`: term, variable, the deviation of the +/-EVENT_SD event and
# its label.
form_arms <- function(form) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    tibble::tibble(variable = v, suffix = form[[v]], term = paste0("dev", v, form[[v]]),
                   positive = grepl("_pos", form[[v]]))
  })) %>%
    mutate(x = ifelse(positive, EVENT_SD, -EVENT_SD),
           value = mapply(term_value, suffix, x),
           label = paste0(ifelse(variable == "TM", "T, ", "P, "),
                          ifelse(variable == "TM", ifelse(positive, "hot", "cold"),
                                 ifelse(positive, "wet", "dry")),
                          sprintf(" year (%+d SD)", x)))
}
response_arms <- form_arms(preferred_form)

# Step 1: one coefficient per country and arm.
country_model <- fit_model(c(sprintf("i(GID_0, %s)", response_arms$term), CONTROLS), preferred_data)
country_V <- stats::vcov(country_model, vcov = "hetero")
arm_years <- preferred_data %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(response_arms$term), ~ sum(.x != 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-GID_0, names_to = "term", values_to = "arm_years")
country_moderators <- distinct(preferred_data, GID_0, clim_TM, clim_RR, inc, inc_level)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(country_moderators$GID_0))
country_slopes <- tibble::tibble(name = grep("^GID_0::", names(stats::coef(country_model)), value = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(GID_0 = sub("^GID_0::([^:]+):.*$", "\\1", name),
         term = sub("^GID_0::[^:]+:", "", name),
         estimate = stats::coef(country_model)[name],
         variance = diag(country_V)[name]) %>%
  left_join(arm_years, by = c("GID_0", "term")) %>%
  left_join(country_moderators, by = "GID_0") %>%
  left_join(select(response_arms, term, variable), by = "term") %>%
  mutate(climate = ifelse(variable == "TM", clim_TM, clim_RR)) %>%
  filter(arm_years >= MIN_ARM_YEARS, is.finite(variance), variance > 0)

# Step 2: the meta-regression of each arm, on climate and income (and on
# climate alone, for comparison).
meta_fits <- lapply(stats::setNames(response_arms$term, response_arms$term), function(a) {
  s <- filter(country_slopes, term == a)
  fit <- function(mods, method) {
    metafor::rma(yi = estimate, vi = variance, mods = mods, data = s, slab = GID_0, method = method)
  }
  list(income = fit(~climate + inc, "REML"), climate = fit(~climate, "REML"),
       income_ml = fit(~climate + inc, "ML"), climate_ml = fit(~climate, "ML"))
})

# 1. The gradients (in pp of the +/-3 SD event, per C or m of long-run climate
# and per log point of income).
pooled_ct <- fixest::coeftable(preferred)
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  f <- meta_fits[[ai$term]]
  k <- 100 * ai$value
  terms <- rownames(pooled_ct)
  clim_term <- interaction_name(ai$term, paste0("clim_", ai$variable), terms)
  inc_term <- interaction_name(ai$term, "inc", terms)
  lr <- stats::anova(f$climate_ml, f$income_ml)
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = ai$label, countries = f$income$k,
    pooled_b = coef_cell(k * pooled_ct[clim_term, 1], k * pooled_ct[clim_term, 2]),
    pooled_h = coef_cell(k * pooled_ct[inc_term, 1], k * pooled_ct[inc_term, 2]),
    meta_b = coef_cell(k * f$income$beta[2], k * f$income$se[2]),
    meta_h = coef_cell(k * f$income$beta[3], k * f$income$se[3]),
    meta_b_without_income = coef_cell(k * f$climate$beta[2], k * f$climate$se[2]),
    tau = signif(k * sqrt(f$income$tau2), 2), I2_pct = round(f$income$I2, 1),
    tau2_explained_by_income_pct = round(100 * (1 - f$income$tau2 / f$climate$tau2), 1),
    no_spread_p = signif(f$income$QEp, 2),
    delta_aic = round(lr$fit.stats.f[["AIC"]] - lr$fit.stats.r[["AIC"]], 1),
    delta_bic = round(lr$fit.stats.f[["BIC"]] - lr$fit.stats.r[["BIC"]], 1),
    income_lr_p = signif(lr$pval, 2)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, %s, horizon deviations: each arm's gradient, pooled (the preferred specification, clustered",
    "SE) and from the meta-regression of the country coefficients (SE), with and without income;",
    "b per C or m of long-run climate and h per log point of income, in pp of the +/-3 SD event;",
    "tau (pp), the SD of the country responses around the gradient; I2 (%%); no_spread_p: the test",
    "that tau = 0; delta AIC and BIC (ML fits, with income minus without) and the likelihood-ratio",
    "test of income; across the countries, correlation of income with mean T %.2f, with mean P %.2f"),
    main$label, PREFERRED_FORM,
    stats::cor(country_moderators$inc, country_moderators$clim_TM),
    stats::cor(country_moderators$inc, country_moderators$clim_RR)))

# 2. Effects at each climate at the average income: pooled CI, meta CI and
# prediction interval (pp).
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  terms <- names(stats::coef(preferred))
  clim <- EVAL_CLIMATE[[ai$variable]]
  G <- t(vapply(clim, function(m) {
    deviation_weights(terms, ai$suffix, ai$variable, ai$x,
                      stats::setNames(list(m, 0), c(paste0("clim_", ai$variable), "inc")))
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  pooled <- linear_combination(preferred, G)
  p <- stats::predict(meta_fits[[ai$term]]$income, newmods = cbind(clim, 0))
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = ai$label, climate = EVAL_LABELS[[ai$variable]],
    pooled_ci = pp_interval(pooled$estimate, pooled$conf_low, pooled$conf_high),
    meta_ci = pp_interval(ai$value * p$pred, ai$value * p$ci.lb, ai$value * p$ci.ub),
    meta_prediction = pp_interval(ai$value * p$pred, ai$value * p$pi.lb, ai$value * p$pi.ub),
    prediction_vs_pooled = round(ai$value * (p$pi.ub - p$pi.lb) /
                                   (pooled$conf_high - pooled$conf_low), 1)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    paste0(main$label, ":"), "effect (pp) of a year at +/-3 SD at each long-run climate and the average",
    "income: the pooled model (95% CI), the meta-regression (95% CI) and its 95% prediction interval",
    "for a country with that climate and income; prediction_vs_pooled: the width of the prediction",
    "interval over that of the pooled CI"))
```

```{r mixed-model-figure, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
# 3. The country estimates moved to the average income (minus h inc), the
# gradient at the average income, its 95% CI and the 95% prediction interval.
response_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  s <- filter(country_slopes, term == ai$term)
  grid <- seq(min(s$climate), max(s$climate), length.out = 100)
  p <- stats::predict(meta_fits[[ai$term]]$income, newmods = cbind(grid, 0))
  tibble::tibble(arm = ai$label, climate = grid, estimate = 100 * ai$value * p$pred,
                 ci_low = 100 * ai$value * p$ci.lb, ci_high = 100 * ai$value * p$ci.ub,
                 pi_low = 100 * ai$value * p$pi.lb, pi_high = 100 * ai$value * p$pi.ub)
}))
response_points <- country_slopes %>%
  left_join(select(response_arms, term, label, value), by = "term") %>%
  mutate(h = vapply(term, function(a) meta_fits[[a]]$income$beta[3], 0)) %>%
  transmute(arm = label, climate, estimate = 100 * value * (estimate - h * inc),
            precision = 1 / sqrt(variance * value^2))
# The vertical range: the prediction interval, with some room; the points
# beyond it are not shown.
response_limits <- response_curves %>%
  group_by(arm) %>%
  summarise(low = min(pi_low, pi_high), high = max(pi_low, pi_high), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pad = 0.25 * (high - low), low = low - pad, high = high + pad)
response_points <- response_points %>%
  left_join(response_limits, by = "arm") %>%
  mutate(shown = estimate >= low & estimate <= high)
arm_order <- function(d) mutate(d, arm = factor(arm, levels = response_arms$label))
ggplot(arm_order(response_curves), aes(climate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmin(pi_low, pi_high), ymax = pmax(pi_low, pi_high)),
              fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmin(ci_low, ci_high), ymax = pmax(ci_low, ci_high)),
              fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = arm_order(filter(response_points, shown)), aes(y = estimate, size = precision),
             colour = "grey35", alpha = 0.45, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = estimate), colour = "#2a78d6", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_blank(data = arm_order(response_limits), aes(x = NULL, y = low), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_blank(data = arm_order(response_limits), aes(x = NULL, y = high), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~arm, scales = "free") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Long-run climate of the country (horizon mean; C, or m a year)",
       y = "Effect on growth (pp)",
       title = "Country responses around the climate gradient, at the average income",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", horizon deviations.\nLine: ",
                         "gradient at the average income; dark band: its 95% CI; light band: 95% ",
                         "prediction interval.\nPoints: country estimates moved to the average ",
                         "income (minus h inc; larger: more precise); beyond the vertical range, ",
                         "not shown: ", sum(!response_points$shown), " of ", nrow(response_points), ".")) +
  theme_results() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```

```{r mixed-model-countries}
# A metafor list of predictions as a data frame with the countries as row names.
by_country <- function(x, r) {
  d <- as.data.frame(unclass(x)[c("pred", "se", "pi.lb", "pi.ub")])
  rownames(d) <- as.character(r$slab[r$not.na])
  d
}
# Each country's own response (BLUP) in each arm, its SE, and the weight on its
# own estimate.
country_blups <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  r <- meta_fits[[ai$term]]$income
  b <- by_country(metafor::blup(r), r)
  tibble::tibble(arm = ai$label, term = ai$term, GID_0 = rownames(b), value = ai$value,
                 blup = b$pred, blup_se = b$se, own_weight = r$tau2 / (r$tau2 + r$vi))
}))

# 4. Precision of the own responses: mean rank of the BLUP SE over the arms.
precision_rank <- country_blups %>%
  group_by(arm) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(blup_se)) %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(arms = n(), mean_rank = mean(rank), mean_se_pp = mean(100 * value * blup_se),
            mean_own_weight = mean(own_weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(arms == nrow(response_arms)) %>%
  arrange(mean_rank)
bind_rows(head(precision_rank, 10) %>% mutate(group = "most precise"),
          tail(precision_rank, 10) %>% mutate(group = "least precise")) %>%
  transmute(group, country = countrycode::countrycode(GID_0, "iso3c", "country.name"), GID_0,
            mean_rank = round(mean_rank, 1), mean_se_pp = round(mean_se_pp, 2),
            mean_own_weight = round(mean_own_weight, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "The countries with the most and the least precise own responses (countries in all %d arms,",
    "of %d): mean rank of the BLUP SE over the arms, the mean BLUP SE (pp of the +/-3 SD event) and",
    "the mean weight on the country's own estimate, tau^2 / (tau^2 + v)"),
    nrow(response_arms), nrow(precision_rank)))

# 5. Four countries: the own coefficients, the mixed model and the pooled model.
RESPONSE_COUNTRIES <- c(IND = "India", BRA = "Brazil", USA = "United States", CHN = "China")
# The slope of arm `ai` in model `m` at the moderators `mods` (named list:
# clim_<v>, inc), with its delta-method SE.
moderated_slope <- function(m, ai, mods) {
  b <- stats::coef(m)
  V <- stats::vcov(m)
  idx <- c(ai$term, vapply(names(mods), function(z) interaction_name(ai$term, z, names(b)), ""))
  w <- c(1, unlist(mods))
  c(estimate = sum(w * b[idx]), se = sqrt(drop(t(w) %*% V[idx, idx] %*% w)))
}
RESPONSE_ESTIMATES <- c("Country OLS", "Mixed", "Pooled")
own_responses <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  clim_name <- paste0("clim_", ai$variable)
  bind_rows(lapply(names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES), function(g) {
    moderators <- filter(country_moderators, GID_0 == g)
    own <- filter(country_slopes, term == ai$term, GID_0 == g)
    mixed <- filter(country_blups, term == ai$term, GID_0 == g)
    stopifnot(nrow(own) == 1, nrow(mixed) == 1)
    pooled <- moderated_slope(preferred, ai, stats::setNames(list(moderators[[clim_name]], moderators$inc),
                                                             c(clim_name, "inc")))
    tibble::tibble(GID_0 = g, country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], arm = ai$label, value = ai$value,
                   estimate_type = RESPONSE_ESTIMATES,
                   slope = c(own$estimate, mixed$blup, pooled[["estimate"]]),
                   se = c(sqrt(own$variance), mixed$blup_se, pooled[["se"]]))
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(effect = 100 * value * slope, half = 1.96 * 100 * value * se,
         low = effect - half, high = effect + half)
own_responses %>%
  transmute(country, arm, estimate_type,
            cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", effect, low, high)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = estimate_type, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Effect (pp, 95% interval) of a +/-3 SD year on the country's growth: its own coefficients",
    "(country OLS), its BLUP in the meta-regression on climate and income (mixed), and the pooled",
    "model with climate and income interactions at its climate and income (pooled)"))
```

```{r mixed-model-countries-figure, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8}
ggplot(own_responses %>%
         mutate(country = factor(country, levels = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES),
                arm = factor(arm, levels = response_arms$label),
                estimate_type = factor(estimate_type, levels = rev(RESPONSE_ESTIMATES))),
       aes(effect, estimate_type, colour = estimate_type)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), width = 0, linewidth = 0.7, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  facet_grid(country ~ arm, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(RESPONSE_ESTIMATES), breaks = RESPONSE_ESTIMATES,
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Effect on growth of a +/-3 SD year (pp, 95% interval)", y = NULL,
       title = "Own response of four countries, with climate and income interactions",
       subtitle = paste0(main$label, ", ", PREFERRED_FORM,
                         ", horizon deviations. Country OLS: the country's own coefficients; mixed: ",
                         "its BLUP\n(meta-regression on climate and income); pooled: the preferred ",
                         "specification at its climate and income.")) +
  theme_results() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5))
```

# Further analyses

The analyses built on the preferred specification and the mixed model are
added from here.

## Correlation across arms: the multivariate mixed model

The mixed model above fits each arm on its own, which leaves out two
correlations between the arms of a country:

- in the sampling errors: a country's four step-1 coefficients come from one
  regression, so they are correlated (the 4 x 4 block of the country in the
  step-1 covariance, of which step 2 used only the diagonal);
- in the true responses: a country that loses more than the gradient in hot
  years may lose more in dry years too.

Neither changes much the response to one arm, but both matter for anything
that combines arms (a hot and dry year; a path of deviations; a projection).
Here the four arms are fitted together:

```text
y_i = theta_i + e_i,              e_i ~ N(0, S_i)      y_i: the country's step-1 coefficients (its arms
                                                        with MIN_ARM_YEARS), S_i: their 4 x 4 robust covariance
theta_i = X_i beta + u_i,         u_i ~ N(0, G)        X_i: each arm's c_a + b_a clim + h_a inc;
                                                        G: the 4 x 4 covariance of the true responses
```

estimated by REML (`metafor::rma.mv`, G unstructured). The step-1
coefficients of different countries are taken as independent (they share
only the year effects and the controls). A block of the step-1 covariance that
is not positive definite (fixest repairs the full matrix, not each block) has
its small eigenvalues raised to a floor.

A country's own responses, given the data, are normal:

```text
theta_i | beta, y = X_i beta + A_i (y_i - X_i,obs beta),  A_i = G[, obs] (G[obs, obs] + S_i)^-1
        variance    G - A_i G[obs, ]
```

with `beta` the GLS estimate (covariance from `rma.mv`); its uncertainty adds
`M_i V_beta M_i'`, `M_i = X_i - A_i X_i,obs`. The responses of an arm a
country lacks in step 1 follow from the others through G.

On `r main$label`:

1. the correlations: the median sampling correlation of each pair of arms
   within a country, and the correlations of the true responses (G), with the
   test that G is diagonal (likelihood ratio);
2. each arm's gradient and spread, arm by arm and jointly;
3. the own responses of India, Brazil, the United States and China, arm by arm
   and jointly.

```{r multivariate-mixed}
# The countries' step-1 coefficients, in the order of the arms within each country.
mv_data <- country_slopes %>%
  mutate(term = factor(term, levels = response_arms$term)) %>%
  arrange(GID_0, term)
mv_countries <- unique(mv_data$GID_0)
# Each country's block of the step-1 covariance, positive definite.
PD_FLOOR <- 1e-8
mv_floored <- 0L
mv_blocks <- lapply(stats::setNames(mv_countries, mv_countries), function(g) {
  nm <- mv_data$name[mv_data$GID_0 == g]
  e <- eigen(country_V[nm, nm, drop = FALSE], symmetric = TRUE)
  floor <- PD_FLOOR * max(e$values)
  if (any(e$values < floor)) mv_floored <<- mv_floored + 1L
  S <- e$vectors %*% diag(pmax(e$values, floor), length(e$values)) %*% t(e$vectors)
  dimnames(S) <- list(as.character(mv_data$term[mv_data$GID_0 == g]),
                      as.character(mv_data$term[mv_data$GID_0 == g]))
  S
})
# The moderators of each arm as columns: the arm, its climate and income terms.
mv_columns <- as.vector(t(outer(response_arms$term, c("", "_clim", "_inc"), paste0)))
mv_design <- function(term, climate, inc) {
  X <- matrix(0, length(term), length(mv_columns), dimnames = list(as.character(term), mv_columns))
  for (k in seq_along(term)) {
    a <- as.character(term[k])
    X[k, paste0(a, c("", "_clim", "_inc"))] <- c(1, climate[k], inc[k])
  }
  X
}
mv_data <- bind_cols(mv_data, as.data.frame(mv_design(mv_data$term, mv_data$climate, mv_data$inc)))
mv_formula <- stats::as.formula(paste("~ 0 +", paste0("`", mv_columns, "`", collapse = " + ")))
mv_fit_struct <- function(struct) {
  metafor::rma.mv(yi = estimate, V = metafor::bldiag(mv_blocks), mods = mv_formula,
                  random = ~ term | GID_0, struct = struct, data = mv_data, method = "REML")
}
mv_fit <- mv_fit_struct("UN")
mv_fit_diagonal <- mv_fit_struct("DIAG")
mv_beta <- stats::coef(mv_fit)
names(mv_beta) <- gsub("`", "", names(mv_beta))
mv_V_beta <- stats::vcov(mv_fit)
dimnames(mv_V_beta) <- list(names(mv_beta), names(mv_beta))
stopifnot(identical(names(mv_beta), mv_columns))
mv_G <- mv_fit$G
dimnames(mv_G) <- list(levels(mv_data$term), levels(mv_data$term))

# 1. Correlations: sampling (median over the countries with both arms) and of
# the true responses (G).
arm_label <- stats::setNames(response_arms$label, response_arms$term)
arm_pairs <- utils::combn(response_arms$term, 2, simplify = FALSE)
bind_rows(lapply(arm_pairs, function(p) {
  sampling <- vapply(mv_blocks, function(S) {
    if (all(p %in% rownames(S))) S[p[1], p[2]] / sqrt(S[p[1], p[1]] * S[p[2], p[2]]) else NA_real_
  }, 0)
  tibble::tibble(arms = paste(arm_label[[p[1]]], "&", arm_label[[p[2]]]),
                 countries = sum(is.finite(sampling)),
                 sampling_median = round(stats::median(sampling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                 sampling_p10_p90 = paste(round(stats::quantile(sampling, c(0.1, 0.9), na.rm = TRUE), 2),
                                          collapse = " .. "),
                 true_responses = round(mv_G[p[1], p[2]] / sqrt(mv_G[p[1], p[1]] * mv_G[p[2], p[2]]), 2))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s: correlation of each pair of arms in the sampling errors of a country's step-1 coefficients",
    "(median and 10th-90th percentiles over the countries with both arms) and in the true country",
    "responses (G, multivariate meta-regression); G diagonal against unstructured: likelihood-ratio",
    "test p = %.2g; step-1 blocks raised to positive definite: %d of %d"),
    main$label, stats::anova(mv_fit, mv_fit_diagonal)$pval, mv_floored, length(mv_blocks)))

# 2. The gradients and spreads, arm by arm and jointly (pp of the +/-3 SD event).
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  f <- meta_fits[[ai$term]]$income
  k <- 100 * ai$value
  b <- paste0(ai$term, "_clim")
  h <- paste0(ai$term, "_inc")
  tibble::tibble(
    arm = ai$label,
    b_by_arm = coef_cell(k * f$beta[2], k * f$se[2]),
    b_joint = coef_cell(k * mv_beta[[b]], k * sqrt(mv_V_beta[b, b])),
    h_by_arm = coef_cell(k * f$beta[3], k * f$se[3]),
    h_joint = coef_cell(k * mv_beta[[h]], k * sqrt(mv_V_beta[h, h])),
    tau_by_arm = signif(k * sqrt(f$tau2), 2),
    tau_joint = signif(k * sqrt(mv_G[ai$term, ai$term]), 2)
  )
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Each arm's gradient in long-run climate (b, per C or m) and income (h, per log point) and the",
    "spread of the country responses (tau), arm by arm and in the multivariate meta-regression;",
    "pp of the +/-3 SD event (SE)"))

# Each country's quantities for its own responses (all arms): the design, its
# observed arms, A_i and the conditional covariance G - A_i G[, obs]'.
mv_country_parts <- lapply(stats::setNames(mv_countries, mv_countries), function(g) {
  d <- mv_data[mv_data$GID_0 == g, ]
  m <- country_moderators[country_moderators$GID_0 == g, ]
  climate <- ifelse(response_arms$variable == "TM", m$clim_TM, m$clim_RR)
  X <- mv_design(response_arms$term, climate, rep(m$inc, nrow(response_arms)))
  obs <- as.character(d$term)
  A <- mv_G[, obs, drop = FALSE] %*% solve(mv_G[obs, obs, drop = FALSE] + mv_blocks[[g]])
  list(y = d$estimate, X = X, X_obs = X[obs, , drop = FALSE], A = A,
       C = mv_G - A %*% mv_G[obs, , drop = FALSE])
})
# The own responses (BLUPs) and their covariance, with the uncertainty of beta.
mv_own <- function(g) {
  p <- mv_country_parts[[g]]
  theta <- drop(p$X %*% mv_beta + p$A %*% (p$y - p$X_obs %*% mv_beta))
  M <- p$X - p$A %*% p$X_obs
  V <- p$C + M %*% mv_V_beta %*% t(M)
  list(theta = theta, V = V)
}

# 3. Four countries, arm by arm and jointly.
bind_rows(lapply(names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES), function(g) {
  own <- mv_own(g)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
    ai <- response_arms[i, ]
    by_arm <- filter(country_blups, GID_0 == g, term == ai$term)
    k <- ai$value
    tibble::tibble(
      country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], arm = ai$label,
      by_arm = if (nrow(by_arm)) pp_interval(k * by_arm$blup, k * (by_arm$blup - 1.96 * by_arm$blup_se),
                                             k * (by_arm$blup + 1.96 * by_arm$blup_se)) else NA_character_,
      joint = pp_interval(k * own$theta[[i]], k * (own$theta[[i]] - 1.96 * sqrt(own$V[i, i])),
                          k * (own$theta[[i]] + 1.96 * sqrt(own$V[i, i])))
    )
  }))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Own response (pp, 95% interval) of a +/-3 SD year: the BLUP of the meta-regression of each arm",
    "on its own and of the multivariate meta-regression (with the uncertainty of the gradient)"))
```

## Draws of the country responses

Draws of every country's four responses, for the analyses that combine arms or
countries. In each draw the gradient is drawn once and shared by every
country, then each country's four deviations are drawn together given it:

```text
beta ~ N(beta_hat, V_beta)
theta_i | beta, y ~ N( X_i beta + A_i (y_i - X_i,obs beta),  G - A_i G[obs, ] )
```

A shared draw of the gradient keeps the correlation across countries that
comes from it (a total over countries is not an average of independent
errors), and the joint draw of a country's arms keeps their correlation. G is
held at its estimate, so the draws leave out the uncertainty of the spread
itself (somewhat narrow for the least precise countries, which lean most on
the gradient). The draws (`r format(2000, big.mark = ",")`, in pp of a 1 SD
deviation of each arm) are saved to
`results/country_responses/country_response_draws.rds`.

1. check: the mean and SD of the draws against the BLUPs and their SEs, for
   the four countries;
2. a hot and dry year (+3 SD T, -3 SD P) in the four countries: from the joint
   draws, and from draws of the arm-by-arm meta-regressions taken as
   independent (each arm its own gradient draw, no correlation between arms).

```{r country-draws}
N_DRAWS <- 2000
DRAW_SEED <- 20261020
# A square root of a covariance matrix (eigenvalues floored at zero).
matrix_root <- function(C) {
  e <- eigen(C, symmetric = TRUE)
  e$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(pmax(e$values, 0)), length(e$values))
}
# Draws of theta (countries x arms x draws), in coefficient units (per SD of
# the arm).
draw_country_responses <- function(n, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  B <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, mv_beta, mv_V_beta)   # n x p
  out <- array(NA_real_, c(length(mv_countries), nrow(response_arms), n),
               dimnames = list(mv_countries, response_arms$term, NULL))
  for (g in mv_countries) {
    p <- mv_country_parts[[g]]
    mean_theta <- p$X %*% t(B) + p$A %*% (p$y - p$X_obs %*% t(B))   # arms x n
    out[g, , ] <- mean_theta + matrix_root(p$C) %*% matrix(stats::rnorm(nrow(response_arms) * n),
                                                           nrow(response_arms))
  }
  out
}
country_draws <- draw_country_responses(N_DRAWS, DRAW_SEED)
dir.create(file.path("results", "country_responses"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(list(draws_pp_per_sd = 100 * country_draws, arms = response_arms,
             moderators = country_moderators, beta = mv_beta, V_beta = mv_V_beta, G = mv_G,
             seed = DRAW_SEED, panel = main$label, form = PREFERRED_FORM),
        file.path("results", "country_responses", "country_response_draws.rds"))

# 1. Check: draws against the BLUPs (pp of the +/-3 SD event).
bind_rows(lapply(names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES), function(g) {
  own <- mv_own(g)
  tibble::tibble(country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]], arm = response_arms$label,
                 blup = round(100 * response_arms$value * own$theta, 2),
                 draws_mean = round(100 * response_arms$value * rowMeans(country_draws[g, , ]), 2),
                 blup_se = round(100 * response_arms$value * sqrt(diag(own$V)), 2),
                 draws_sd = round(100 * response_arms$value * apply(country_draws[g, , ], 1, stats::sd), 2))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Check of the %s draws: the BLUP of the multivariate meta-regression and its SE against the mean",
    "and SD of the draws (pp of the +/-3 SD event)"), format(N_DRAWS, big.mark = ",")))

# Draws of the arm-by-arm meta-regressions, each arm on its own (its own
# gradient draw; arms independent): countries x draws for arm a.
draw_by_arm <- function(a, n) {
  fit <- meta_fits[[a]]$income
  B <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, stats::coef(fit), stats::vcov(fit))
  fitted <- fit$X %*% t(B)
  lambda <- fit$tau2 / (fit$tau2 + fit$vi)
  u <- lambda * (fit$yi - fitted) +
    sqrt(lambda * fit$vi) * matrix(stats::rnorm(length(fitted)), nrow(fitted))
  out <- fitted + u
  rownames(out) <- as.character(fit$slab[fit$not.na])
  out
}
set.seed(DRAW_SEED + 1)
by_arm_draws <- lapply(stats::setNames(response_arms$term, response_arms$term), draw_by_arm, N_DRAWS)

# 2. A hot and dry year.
HOT_DRY <- c(devTM_pos = 3, devRR_neg = 3)   # values of the arms at +3 SD T, -3 SD P
interval_cell <- function(x) {
  q <- stats::quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), names = FALSE)
  sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]", q[2], q[1], q[3])
}
bind_rows(lapply(names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES), function(g) {
  joint_draws <- 100 * colSums(HOT_DRY * country_draws[g, names(HOT_DRY), ])
  arm_draws <- if (all(vapply(names(HOT_DRY), function(a) g %in% rownames(by_arm_draws[[a]]), TRUE))) {
    100 * Reduce(`+`, lapply(names(HOT_DRY), function(a) HOT_DRY[[a]] * by_arm_draws[[a]][g, ]))
  } else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[[g]],
                 joint = interval_cell(joint_draws), by_arm_independent = interval_cell(arm_draws),
                 sd_joint = round(stats::sd(joint_draws), 2), sd_by_arm = round(stats::sd(arm_draws), 2))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "A hot and dry year (+3 SD temperature, -3 SD precipitation): effect on growth (pp; median and",
    "95% interval of the draws) from the joint draws of the multivariate meta-regression and from the",
    "arm-by-arm meta-regressions drawn independently; and the SD of each"))
```


## Export for an integrated assessment model

The multivariate mixed model is saved as CSV files for implementation in an
integrated assessment model. There are two versions, each with its own
specification (`README.md`):

- **climate and income** (`results/iam_handout/`): the model above, with each
  arm's gradient in the long-run climate and income;
- **climate only** (`results/iam_handout_climate_only/`): the same step-1
  coefficients, with each arm's gradient in the long-run climate alone (no
  income in the meta-regression).

Each country's response is split into the gradient, which moves with the
country's moderators, and the country's own deviation from it, which does not:

```text
theta_i(t) = X(clim_i(t) [, inc_i(t)]) beta + u_i
u_i | beta, y = a_i - D_i beta + e_i,   e_i ~ N(0, C_i)      a_i = A_i y_i, D_i = A_i X_i,obs
```

A country without step-1 coefficients (not in the sample) has `u_i ~ N(0, G)`.
The draws share one gradient draw across countries, as in "Draws of the
country responses". The checks rebuild each country's response from the
exported pieces. For the model with income they compare it with `mv_own()`;
for the climate-only model they compare the own deviations with metafor's
(`ranef`). The table compares the two models: each arm's climate gradient, its
spread, and the likelihood-ratio test of the four income terms (ML fits).

```{r iam-export}
IAM_DRAWS <- 1000
IAM_SEED <- 20261022
arm_names <- response_arms$term

# The climate-only multivariate meta-regression (step 1 as above).
mv_columns_climate <- as.vector(t(outer(response_arms$term, c("", "_clim"), paste0)))
mv_fit_climate <- metafor::rma.mv(
  yi = estimate, V = metafor::bldiag(mv_blocks),
  mods = stats::as.formula(paste("~ 0 +", paste0("`", mv_columns_climate, "`", collapse = " + "))),
  random = ~ term | GID_0, struct = "UN", data = mv_data, method = "REML")

# The pieces of a fitted multivariate meta-regression `fit` with the moderator
# columns `suffixes` per arm ("" the constant, "_clim", "_inc"): beta, its
# covariance, G, the design at given moderators, and each country's a_i, D_i,
# C_i (u_i = a_i - D_i beta + e_i, e_i ~ N(0, C_i)).
mixed_parts <- function(fit, suffixes) {
  beta <- stats::coef(fit)
  names(beta) <- gsub("`", "", names(beta))
  columns <- as.vector(t(outer(arm_names, suffixes, paste0)))
  stopifnot(identical(names(beta), columns))
  V_beta <- stats::vcov(fit)
  dimnames(V_beta) <- list(columns, columns)
  G <- fit$G
  dimnames(G) <- list(levels(mv_data$term), levels(mv_data$term))
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(G), arm_names))
  # Rows: arms; columns: beta. `climate` and `inc` per arm.
  design <- function(climate, inc) {
    X <- matrix(0, length(arm_names), length(columns), dimnames = list(arm_names, columns))
    for (k in seq_along(arm_names)) {
      values <- c(1, climate[[k]], inc[[k]])[match(suffixes, c("", "_clim", "_inc"))]
      X[k, paste0(arm_names[[k]], suffixes)] <- values
    }
    X
  }
  country_design <- function(g) {
    m <- country_moderators[country_moderators$GID_0 == g, ]
    design(ifelse(response_arms$variable == "TM", m$clim_TM, m$clim_RR), rep(m$inc, length(arm_names)))
  }
  parts <- lapply(stats::setNames(mv_countries, mv_countries), function(g) {
    d <- mv_data[mv_data$GID_0 == g, ]
    obs <- as.character(d$term)
    X <- country_design(g)
    A <- G[, obs, drop = FALSE] %*% solve(G[obs, obs, drop = FALSE] + mv_blocks[[g]])
    C <- G - A %*% G[obs, , drop = FALSE]
    list(a = drop(A %*% d$estimate), D = A %*% X[obs, , drop = FALSE], C = (C + t(C)) / 2, X = X)
  })
  list(beta = beta, V_beta = V_beta, G = G, suffixes = suffixes, design = design, parts = parts)
}
IAM_MODELS <- list(
  "climate and income" = list(dir = file.path("results", "iam_handout"),
                              parts = mixed_parts(mv_fit, c("", "_clim", "_inc"))),
  "climate only" = list(dir = file.path("results", "iam_handout_climate_only"),
                        parts = mixed_parts(mv_fit_climate, c("", "_clim")))
)

# The pieces match the model with income (mv_own) and the climate-only fit
# (metafor's own deviations of the observed arms).
local({
  p <- IAM_MODELS[["climate and income"]]$parts
  for (g in mv_countries) {
    o <- p$parts[[g]]
    own <- mv_own(g)
    M <- o$X - o$D
    stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(drop(o$X %*% p$beta + o$a - o$D %*% p$beta)), unname(own$theta))),
              isTRUE(all.equal(unname(o$C + M %*% p$V_beta %*% t(M)), unname(own$V))))
  }
  p <- IAM_MODELS[["climate only"]]$parts
  r <- metafor::ranef(mv_fit_climate)[[1]]
  u_metafor <- stats::setNames(r$intrcpt, gsub(" ", "", rownames(r)))
  u_parts <- unlist(lapply(mv_countries, function(g) {
    o <- p$parts[[g]]
    stats::setNames(drop(o$a - o$D %*% p$beta), paste0(arm_names, "|", g))
  }))
  stopifnot(all(names(u_metafor) %in% names(u_parts)),
            isTRUE(all.equal(unname(u_parts[names(u_metafor)]), unname(u_metafor), tolerance = 1e-6)))
})

# The countries: moderators, horizon moments, the variability of the
# deviations on the sample rows, and the sample flags.
moments <- main$data %>%
  filter(!is.na(sd_TM_all), !is.na(sd_RR_all)) %>%
  distinct(GID_0, mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(moments$GID_0))
variability <- preferred_data %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(sample_years = n(), first_year = min(year), last_year = max(year),
            sd_dT = stats::sd(devTM), sd_dP = stats::sd(devRR),
            mean_devTM_pos = mean(devTM_pos), mean_devTM_neg = mean(devTM_neg),
            mean_devRR_pos = mean(devRR_pos), mean_devRR_neg = mean(devRR_neg), .groups = "drop")
countries_all <- country_moderators %>%
  transmute(GID_0, country = countrycode::countrycode(GID_0, "iso3c", "country.name", warn = FALSE),
            clim_TM, clim_RR, log_gdp_pc = inc_level, gdp_pc = exp(inc_level), inc,
            in_meta_regression = GID_0 %in% mv_countries,
            arms_estimated = vapply(GID_0, function(g) {
              paste(as.character(mv_data$term[mv_data$GID_0 == g]), collapse = ";")
            }, "")) %>%
  left_join(moments, by = "GID_0") %>%
  left_join(variability, by = "GID_0")
income_centre <- mean(preferred_data$inc_level)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(preferred_data$inc, preferred_data$inc_level - income_centre)))
units <- distinct(preferred_data, GID_0, clim_TM, clim_RR, inc)

# Writes the handout of model `p` (mixed_parts) to `dir`.
export_iam <- function(p, dir) {
  with_income <- "_inc" %in% p$suffixes
  dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  out <- function(x, file) utils::write.csv(x, file.path(dir, file), row.names = FALSE)
  out(response_arms %>%
        transmute(arm = term, variable, side = ifelse(positive, "positive", "negative"),
                  description = sub(" year.*$", " year", label),
                  arm_value = ifelse(positive, "max(d, 0)", "max(-d, 0)"),
                  climate_moderator = paste0("clim_", variable),
                  climate_unit = ifelse(variable == "TM", "C", "m per year")), "arms.csv")
  # 1. The gradient and its covariance; 2. the spread G.
  out(tibble::tibble(
    parameter = names(p$beta), arm = sub("_(clim|inc)$", "", names(p$beta)),
    moderator = ifelse(grepl("_clim$", names(p$beta)), "clim",
                       ifelse(grepl("_inc$", names(p$beta)), "inc", "constant")),
    estimate = unname(p$beta), std_error = sqrt(diag(p$V_beta))), "gradient_beta.csv")
  out(data.frame(parameter = names(p$beta), p$V_beta, check.names = FALSE), "gradient_vcov.csv")
  out(data.frame(arm = rownames(p$G), p$G, check.names = FALSE), "spread_G.csv")
  # 3. Each country's own deviation.
  out(bind_rows(lapply(mv_countries, function(g) {
    o <- p$parts[[g]]
    D <- o$D
    colnames(D) <- paste0("D_", colnames(D))
    tibble::tibble(GID_0 = g, arm = arm_names, a = o$a, u_mean = drop(o$a - o$D %*% p$beta)) %>%
      bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(D))
  })), "country_deviation.csv")
  out(bind_rows(lapply(mv_countries, function(g) {
    C <- p$parts[[g]]$C
    expand.grid(row = arm_names, col = arm_names, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      transmute(GID_0 = g, row, col, cov = C[cbind(row, col)])
  })), "country_deviation_cov.csv")
  # 4. The countries (without the income columns in the climate-only model).
  out(if (with_income) countries_all else select(countries_all, -log_gdp_pc, -gdp_pc, -inc),
      "countries.csv")
  # 5. Constants and the support of the sample.
  constants <- tibble::tribble(
    ~item, ~value, ~note,
    "model", if (with_income) "climate and income" else "climate only",
    "moderators of each arm's gradient in the meta-regression",
    "panel", main$label, "PWT 11.0 rgdpna/pop; ERA5, population-density weights (2000)",
    "horizon", paste(START_YEAR, main$end_year, sep = "-"), "years of the climate moments, the income and the sample",
    "observations", as.character(nrow(preferred_data)), "country-years of the regression",
    "countries_in_sample", as.character(n_distinct(preferred_data$GID_0)), "",
    "countries_in_meta_regression", as.character(length(mv_countries)), "with at least one arm in step 2",
    "min_arm_years", as.character(MIN_ARM_YEARS), "years with the arm non-zero for a country-arm to enter step 2",
    "income_centre_log_gdp_pc", format(income_centre, digits = 10), "inc = log(GDP per capita) - this",
    "income_unit", "2021 PPP international dollars (PWT rgdpna / pop)", "",
    "clim_TM_min", format(min(units$clim_TM), digits = 6), "support of the countries' long-run temperature (C)",
    "clim_TM_max", format(max(units$clim_TM), digits = 6), "",
    "clim_RR_min", format(min(units$clim_RR), digits = 6), "support of the countries' long-run precipitation (m per year)",
    "clim_RR_max", format(max(units$clim_RR), digits = 6), "",
    "inc_min", format(min(units$inc), digits = 6), "support of the countries' centred log income",
    "inc_max", format(max(units$inc), digits = 6), "",
    "dT_min", format(min(preferred_data$devTM), digits = 6), "support of the demeaned temperature deviation (SD)",
    "dT_max", format(max(preferred_data$devTM), digits = 6), "",
    "dP_min", format(min(preferred_data$devRR), digits = 6), "support of the demeaned precipitation deviation (SD)",
    "dP_max", format(max(preferred_data$devRR), digits = 6), "",
    "draws", as.character(IAM_DRAWS), "joint draws of beta and u in draws_beta.csv and draws_u.csv",
    "seed", as.character(IAM_SEED), "R set.seed() before MASS::mvrnorm and stats::rnorm"
  )
  if (!with_income) constants <- filter(constants, !grepl("^(income_|inc_)", item))
  out(constants, "constants.csv")
  # 6. Joint draws: beta shared by the countries, then each country's u given it.
  set.seed(IAM_SEED)
  beta_draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(IAM_DRAWS, p$beta, p$V_beta)
  colnames(beta_draws) <- names(p$beta)
  out(data.frame(draw = seq_len(IAM_DRAWS), beta_draws, check.names = FALSE), "draws_beta.csv")
  u_draws <- bind_rows(lapply(mv_countries, function(g) {
    o <- p$parts[[g]]
    u <- o$a - o$D %*% t(beta_draws) +
      matrix_root(o$C) %*% matrix(stats::rnorm(length(arm_names) * IAM_DRAWS), length(arm_names))
    tibble::tibble(draw = seq_len(IAM_DRAWS), GID_0 = g) %>%
      bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(stats::setNames(as.data.frame(t(u)), arm_names)))
  }))
  out(u_draws, "draws_u.csv")
  # 7. Validation: each country's response at its own moderators, its total
  # SD, and the mean and SD of the draws.
  validation <- bind_rows(lapply(mv_countries, function(g) {
    o <- p$parts[[g]]
    theta <- drop(o$X %*% p$beta + o$a - o$D %*% p$beta)
    M <- o$X - o$D
    draws_theta <- o$X %*% t(beta_draws) + t(as.matrix(u_draws[u_draws$GID_0 == g, arm_names]))
    v <- tibble::tibble(GID_0 = g, arm = arm_names,
                        clim = o$X[cbind(arm_names, paste0(arm_names, "_clim"))])
    if (with_income) v$inc <- o$X[cbind(arm_names, paste0(arm_names, "_inc"))]
    mutate(v, theta_mean = theta, theta_sd = sqrt(diag(o$C + M %*% p$V_beta %*% t(M))),
           draws_mean = rowMeans(draws_theta), draws_sd = apply(draws_theta, 1, stats::sd),
           effect_3sd_pp = 100 * 3 * theta)
  }))
  out(validation, "validation.csv")
  validation
}
iam_validation <- lapply(IAM_MODELS, function(m) export_iam(m$parts, m$dir))

# 1. The two models: each arm's climate gradient and spread (pp of the 3 SD
# event), and the likelihood-ratio test of the income terms (ML fits).
ml <- function(columns) {
  metafor::rma.mv(yi = estimate, V = metafor::bldiag(mv_blocks),
                  mods = stats::as.formula(paste("~ 0 +", paste0("`", columns, "`", collapse = " + "))),
                  random = ~ term | GID_0, struct = "UN", data = mv_data, method = "ML")
}
income_lr <- stats::anova(ml(mv_columns), ml(mv_columns_climate))
bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(response_arms)), function(i) {
  ai <- response_arms[i, ]
  k <- 100 * unname(ai$value)
  b <- paste0(ai$term, "_clim")
  cells <- lapply(IAM_MODELS, function(m) {
    p <- m$parts
    c(b = coef_cell(k * p$beta[[b]], k * sqrt(p$V_beta[b, b])),
      constant = coef_cell(k * p$beta[[ai$term]], k * sqrt(p$V_beta[ai$term, ai$term])),
      tau = signif(k * sqrt(p$G[ai$term, ai$term]), 2))
  })
  tibble::tibble(arm = ai$label,
                 b_with_income = cells[[1]][["b"]], b_climate_only = cells[[2]][["b"]],
                 constant_climate_only = cells[[2]][["constant"]],
                 tau_with_income = cells[[1]][["tau"]], tau_climate_only = cells[[2]][["tau"]])
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "%s, multivariate meta-regression with climate and income and with climate only: each arm's",
    "climate gradient b (per C or m of long-run climate) and, climate only, its constant (at a",
    "long-run climate of 0), in pp of the 3 SD event (SE); tau, the SD of the country responses",
    "around the gradient (pp). The four income terms: likelihood-ratio test p = %.2g (ML fits;",
    "AIC with income minus without %.1f, BIC %.1f)"),
    main$label, income_lr$pval, income_lr$fit.stats.f[["AIC"]] - income_lr$fit.stats.r[["AIC"]],
    income_lr$fit.stats.f[["BIC"]] - income_lr$fit.stats.r[["BIC"]]))

# 2. Check of the exports: four countries, each arm at its own moderators.
bind_rows(lapply(names(iam_validation), function(k) {
  iam_validation[[k]] %>%
    filter(GID_0 %in% names(RESPONSE_COUNTRIES)) %>%
    transmute(model = k, country = RESPONSE_COUNTRIES[GID_0], arm = arm_label[arm],
              cell = sprintf("%+.2f (%.2f; draws %+.2f, %.2f)", effect_3sd_pp, 300 * theta_sd,
                             300 * draws_mean, 300 * draws_sd))
})) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Check of the exports: the response of four countries to a 3 SD event of each arm at their own",
    "climate (and income), rebuilt from the CSV pieces, pp (total SD; mean and SD of the %s draws)"),
    format(IAM_DRAWS, big.mark = ",")))
```
